A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same dense-associative-memory study. Their complete text, equations and figures support comparison, including v2's Appendices A–C. v1 ends with references and has no appendices.

before.justification: Section 5 and Figure 1 give numerical illustrations of theoretical approximate fixed-point equations. v1 reports no experimental study, sampled network simulations or analysis of observed data.

after.justification: Section 5.1 and Figures 1–2 report original network simulations with N=512 and 100 trials, comparing retrieval trajectories and attraction basins with numerical GFA predictions.

M1.justification: The polynomial-energy memory model, binary parallel update rule, GFA framework and approximation neglecting retarded self-interaction are retained. Numerically evaluating the existing exact equations does not introduce a new recall algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions study retrieval of independent, unbiased binary memory patterns from initial states with specified overlaps. The added simulations retain this task and population; network size and interaction-order changes concern experimental settings.

E2.justification: v1 Figure 1 evaluates approximate dynamics alone. v2 Figure 2 explicitly compares full-GFA and network results against the existing zero-retarded-interaction approximation, shown as a red reference curve. This adds a comparative evaluation without introducing an external baseline algorithm.

E3.justification: v2 introduces Monte Carlo evaluation of the full GFA equations and finite-network simulations at N=512, n=3. It evaluates trajectories at loading rates 0.1–0.4 and attraction basins after 200 iterations. v1 instead evaluates approximate fixed points across several interaction orders up to n=20.

E4.justification: v2 adds trajectory analyses across initial overlaps and loading rates, and directly tests the effect of retaining versus neglecting retarded self-interaction through Figure 2. The earlier numerical sensitivity analysis across multiple interaction orders is removed, substantially changing the analytical evidence.

E5.justification: v2 first reports 100 simulation trials in Figures 1–2 and displays error bars in Figure 1. v1 has no repeated-run or uncertainty reporting. The later version does not define whether the bars represent standard deviations, standard errors or confidence intervals.

E6.justification: v2 adds full-GFA and simulation trajectories, basin maps, convergence within several tens of iterations, and a reported n=3 capacity of 0.33. v1's approximate capacity list, including 0.252 for n=3, and higher-order basin curves disappear; the n=3 approximate boundary survives as a reference. The two capacity values come from different analyses, not an unchanged-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: Appendices A–B add combinatorial and saddle-point proof sketches. The pairing coefficient B(m) changes from the even-m indicator times (2m-1)!! to the indicator times (m-1)!!. Conversely, v1 Section 4.3's three stationary-state assumptions, derivation and Proposition 2 are removed. Appendix C largely relocates the earlier Gardner-model Lemma 2 rather than introducing a new result.

C1.justification: v2's abstract and contributions explicitly claim quantitative convergence-time characterization and applicability to other energy-based architectures. The stationary-state solution emphasized in v1 is dropped as a contribution, with the conclusion now describing it as something one can consider. The central exact-GFA claim remains.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new comparisons as showing that retarded self-interaction increases capacity and discusses finite-size discrepancies near basin boundaries. It adds limitations concerning small systems and restricted interaction orders, qualifies the earlier categorical noise statement, and removes the Maxwell-construction interpretation accompanying the stationary-state result.

D1.justification: v2 identifies Monte Carlo as the numerical approach and documents concrete simulation settings, including N=512, n=3 and the 200-step basin evaluation. These are limited reproducibility additions: neither code access nor the Monte Carlo implementation, sample count or hardware is supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds GFA-related references by Düring et al. (1998), Coolen (2000), Mimura et al. (2004), and Mimura and Coolen (2009), while removing Amari and Maginu (1988). Its central positioning relative to Gardner, Abbott and equilibrium analyses remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution statement and conclusion are substantially rewritten. Notation moves into preliminaries, Analysis gains separate path-probability and generating-functional subsections, approximate dynamics and equilibrium comparisons move into Discussion, and derivations are redistributed into appendices.

P2.justification: The single monochrome, multi-order basin plot is replaced by eight trajectory panels and two color basin maps, adding error bars, color scales and an approximation overlay. The document also adopts different title, heading, equation and reference formatting. Neither version contains tables.

improvement.justification: v1 leaves its exact dynamics numerically untested. v2 directly compares full-GFA predictions with network simulations, examines the effect of retarded interaction, corrects the pairing coefficient and supplies substantial proof sketches. These changes strengthen the central dynamical argument enough to outweigh the removed stationary-state derivation and narrower interaction-order coverage. Remaining appendix notation problems and incomplete Monte Carlo/error-bar documentation limit the improvement.
